idiom_name: Django authentication backends (AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS); Protocol + registry for standalone code
implementation_notes: Django's authentication system is the pattern: each backend is a class with authenticate(request, **credentials) and get_user(user_id), listed in AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS, and django.contrib.auth.authenticate() tries them in order until one returns a user - the normalized principal is the User object. Outside Django the idiomatic form is a typing.Protocol plus a registry dict keyed by scheme, wired into framework middleware or dependencies (Starlette/FastAPI, Flask-Login's user_loader); hashing primitives come from passlib or argon2-cffi. Either way a hand-written class hierarchy is unnecessary.
pitfalls: Order and short-circuiting matter: the first backend that returns a user wins, and one that raises PermissionDenied stops the chain.
Django caches the backend that authenticated a user in the session, so changing AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS does not re-authenticate existing sessions until they are flushed.
authenticate() must not be treated as a user-existence oracle - it applies is_active only when the backend does.
Never return a fallback or default user object from a backend that could not verify the credential; that is an authentication bypass.
